messages.author: ae4e3267fde51265
messages.subject: interpreting results
parts:
Dr. Broman, 

I read this in your book somewhere a while back, but I cannot seem to find it anymore. If the result is a marker that is not a named SNP in my dataset, e.g. c2.loc15, how would one interpret these results? Thank you so much! 

> summary(out.hk, perms=operm.hk, alpha=0.05, pvalues=TRUE)
                    chr     pos   lod pval
25.1_CHR_XL_2980405   1   0.285 38.70    0
c2.loc15              2  15.000 19.63    0
c3.loc76              3  76.000 15.87    0
27._CHR_2_27481033    4 115.052  8.67    0

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: interpreting results
parts:
Calculations are performed at the markers as well as at a grid of pseudomarkers (non-marker locations inserted between markers). The pseudomarkers are giving names like "c2.loc15" for chr 2 at position 15 cM.

The summary shows the locations with the maximum LOD score on each chromosome. For some chromosomes, the maximum LOD score occurred at a marker; for other chromosomes it occurred at one of these pseudomarkers.

karl
